Bugfix: two destinations you can never reach
Bugfix: a travel research that does nothing
Bugfix: production and dead ends on the far planets
Content: one more permanent slot, late game

patches.desc:
Gravitational Slingshot, Ring Harmonics and the Storm Core card
   were added to the game without translations, so in six of the
   eight languages they render as raw lookup keys like
   'researches.ring_harmonics.name'. This fills them in with the
   English text - not a translation, but readable. English and
   Chinese already have them and are left alone.
patches.title: Bugfix: untranslated text showing as raw keys

patches.desc:
Acid Clouds (Venus), Martian Dungeons (Mars) and Great Red Spot
   (Jupiter) scale exponentially (x2 to x2.5 per level) and end up
   hundreds of times stronger than the zones that come after them -
   Martian Dungeons' boss is the strongest thing in the game and
   Great Red Spot's level-20 regulars out-stat its own boss 3 to 1.
   This re-slopes them so each is conquerable roughly one planet
   later than where you find it, still growing faster than linear:
   Acid Clouds during Mars, Martian Dungeons during Jupiter/Saturn,
   Great Red Spot as the endgame push at near-max cards & Big Bang.
   Boss attacks are brought down to where HP/defense builds actually
   survive hits (no build in the game can survive a million-attack
   one-shot), and the Martian Dungeons boss finally drops real loot.
patches.title: Rebalance: fix the three impossible challenge zones
Bugfix: a drop card that can never be levelled
Bugfix: a card that fell out of the drop tables
Bugfix: a card that stops dead partway up
Bugfix: two upgrade cards that cannot be levelled
Bugfix: some fights freeze on the enemy's turn
Bugfix: three late researches can never unlock

patches.desc:
Improved Solar Panels on Mars asks for water, and the amount is
   steep next to everything else on the planet: 100,000 per level,
   and the cost climbs with the level, so the full ladder to 100
   wants over half a billion water. Martian Walls is the same
   shape with soil. Both cost less per level now: the solar
   panels drop to 15% of what they were, the walls a fifth off.
   Nothing else about either one changes, and progress is
   stored as a percentage of the cost, so a job you are part
   way through keeps exactly where it was and simply needs
   less to finish.
patches.title: Rebalance: Mars water and soil costs
Rebalance: two late game upgrades
Rebalance: one planet costs more than the next one
Rework: a battle card nobody could use
Rework: three battle cards that stop scaling

patches.desc:
The deck holds 6 cards but the battle hand holds only 5, so one
   random deck card sits out of every fight - which also makes
   passive in-hand cards (Taichi Master, Lightning Action)
   unreliable. This adds a second level to Venus's 'Extra Hand
   Slot' research: research it in-game and your whole deck is in
   hand every battle. Level 1 is unchanged, so nothing is free.
patches.title: QoL: researchable 6th battle hand slot
Content: more Big Bang upgrades
New card: an Epic Action card

patches.desc:
The base game calculates every hit as attack MINUS defense, so
   any hit is either a one-shot or exactly 0 - defense and healing
   are useless until they suddenly make you immortal. This changes
   the rule to: damage = atk x atk / (atk + def). Defense always
   reduces damage by a percentage and never to zero (defense equal
   to the attack halves it). Applies to you AND enemies.
patches.title: Smooth damage formula (fixes zero-or-oneshot combat)

patches.desc:
If you own any of the three beta/contributor medal cards, loading
   a save can dump you into the tutorial with your dark matter
   showing as 0. The game tries to upload your medal 'roles' to the
   developer's server, which the community build cannot reach, and
   the error aborts the rest of the load. Worse, the autosave then
   writes that half-loaded state back, so every later load breaks
   the same way. This skips the upload - there is nothing to upload
   to offline - and lets the load finish normally. The same file
   carries the offline time limit below and the Time away line on
   the Welcome Back panel, so turning this off takes those too.
patches.title: Bugfix: save refuses to load (drops you into the tutorial)

patches.desc:
The base game credits all the time you were away, however long.
   This adds a limit: one day for free, and two cheap lines in the
   Big Bang tree stretch it, up to sixteen weeks. Offline boss
   kills follow the same limit. Turn this off to keep the base
   game's unlimited offline time. The two Big Bang lines then lock,
   since there is nothing for them to raise, and any levels you
   already bought can still be taken back down for a refund. It
   lives inside the save fix above, so it needs that one on.
patches.title: Offline time limit: one day, Big Bang upgrades raise it

patches.desc:
Three small battle bugfixes. (1) In-hand HP buffs (Taichi Master,
   The Bomb) raised your MAX HP but not your current HP, so the
   buff only added empty health bar - current HP now scales with
   it. (2) The battle hand was drawn for 5 cards; with the modded
   6th hand slot the last card clipped into the Skip/Surrender
   buttons - the hand now scales to fit however many cards you have.
   (3) Biomass and stardust drops in the battle log printed raw
   text like 'panels.storage.resources.biomass.name' instead of
   the word. The game looks those two words up once, before its
   own language file is ready, and keeps the failure for the whole
   session - they are now checked and repaired at startup.
patches.title: Battle fixes: HP buffs fill up, 6-card hand fits on screen

patches.desc:
Discarding a card costs your whole turn - the same as Skip,
   except you also lose the card, and with the 6th hand slot the
   discarded card is the only thing that can be redrawn so it comes
   straight back anyway. This removes the trash-can drop zone from
   the battle screen. Skip it if you want to keep vanilla discarding.
patches.title: Remove the discard (trash can) zone from battles

patches.desc:
Adds a MAX button under the forge's Synthesize button. One click
   repeats the synthesis until biomass, stardust or ingredient
   cards run out, then shows how many cards were made and the best
   level rolled. Each craft uses the game's own costs and random
   level roll - it just saves you hundreds of clicks.
   Also adds a DE-LEVEL toggle: when ON, synthesis that is short of
   ingredient cards splits your merged-up copies back down to the
   level the recipe needs (1 card of level N -> 4 of level N-1, the
   exact mirror of merging, so no card value is lost). Never touches
   equipped or protected cards, always keeps one copy of your
   highest level, and charges 10% of the split card's sell value
   in biomass per split.
   Finally, once a recipe has produced a Perfect (max-level) card,
   both Synthesize and MAX refuse that recipe - there is no better
   roll to chase, so your resources stay in the bank.
patches.title: Alchemy forge: 'MAX' button, DE-LEVEL toggle, Perfect guard

patches.desc:
The game hardcodes 2 saved loadouts each for the battle deck and
   the permanent card set, but every save already has room for 100.
   This unlocks one extra loadout slot per planet you reach beyond
   Venus (Mercury: 3 ... Mars: 5 ... Pluto: 10). Slots appear
   automatically as you travel; saves are untouched.
   It also keeps the dropdown that lists them on screen. That
   popup was drawn for three lines, so a longer list either
   ran off the panel and got cut away or had nothing to
   scroll with. One that already fits is left alone.
   A slot you have put cards in or given a name of your own
   stays in the list after a Big Bang, instead of hiding
   until you have flown back out to the planet that unlocked
   it. And the dropdown no longer snaps shut every time a
   research or infrastructure level finishes. Loadouts also
   keep their cards when you level those cards up, instead of
   quietly dropping the ones whose level has changed.
patches.title: More deck & permanent-set loadouts (up to 10 each)

patches.desc:
On the Big Bang upgrades tab, the dark-matter total is drawn on
   top of the bottom-left upgrade item. This parks the total in
   the panel's bottom-left corner and resizes the upgrade list to
   fill everything above it, so every upgrade is fully visible and
   clickable and the freed space is actually used. Measured at
   runtime, and reverted when you leave the tab.
   Also fixes the vanilla bug where the game slows to a crawl and
   stops registering clicks once your research and infrastructure
   are fast: every level writes a message, the game ticks ten
   times a second, and each message rebuilds the whole log's
   layout. Level up messages are now folded together and the log
   is capped, so it cannot grow without limit.
   And it makes a previewed loadout read only. Selecting a
   saved loadout shows you a copy of it, but clicking a card
   in that copy used to take the card out of your live set
   instead, with nothing moving on screen to tell you. The row
   now greys out like the bag beside it already did.
   And the game window opens where you last left it, instead
   of in the same default spot every launch.
patches.title: UI fixes: the Big Bang window, and the message log

patches.desc:
On the beta and beta-danger branches, and on every Mac, the game
   is a Unity DEVELOPMENT build. There any engine error throws a
   black 'Development Console' box across the middle of the screen
   with red text on it. The usual trigger is nothing to do with the
   game: plug in a headset or switch your sound device while playing
   and the audio engine complains. It cannot be dismissed for good.
   It returns on the next error.
   This adds a 'Hide error console' switch to the game's own
   settings, on by default, that keeps the box off the screen.
   On the normal Windows branch the box never appears, so there
   this does nothing and costs nothing.
   Note: the small 'Development Build' watermark in the corner is
   drawn by the engine itself and cannot be removed this way.
patches.title: Hide the developer error console

patches.desc:
Vanilla bug. Finishing a research level makes the game rebuild the
   card loadouts, the research/infra lists, the star strip and the
   destination selector. While a list is being rebuilt it is empty
   for a frame, so Unity snaps it back to the top - and there it
   stays. In the late game research finishes constantly, so long
   lists become almost unreadable. This remembers where every list
   was and puts it back once the rebuild is done. It lets go the
   instant you touch the wheel or drag, so it never fights you.
patches.title: Stop lists jumping back to the top when research completes

patches.desc:
The pop-up that explains an upgrade, a card or a research is
   hardcoded to vanish after five seconds, whether or not you are
   still pointing at it - long descriptions simply cannot be read
   in that time. This adds a 'Tooltip time' row to the game's own
   settings; click it to cycle 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 seconds. It is
   capped at 30 so a tooltip can never get stuck on screen. It
   also fixes a smaller vanilla annoyance: moving onto a second
   thing used to inherit what was left of the first one's five
   seconds, so the second pop-up could vanish almost at once.
patches.title: Choose how long tooltips stay on screen

patches.desc:
The game uses almost no keys at all, so nearly everything you do
   often needs the mouse. This adds shortcuts for the things that
   get repeated: up/down walk the left-hand menu and left/right
   walk the tabs inside a panel, the number keys jump straight to
   a combat zone (Shift for zones 11-20), Ctrl and a number loads
   a deck loadout, and there are keys for auto levelling, auto
   fight, zone level up/down, merge all, the travel destination
   and a quick save. Press F1 in game for the full list. Every
   key can be changed in BepInEx\config\sti.community.hotkeys.cfg,
   and the shortcuts are ignored while you are typing in a name
   or filter box. Departing and quick loading need the key pressed
   twice, so neither can happen by accident. The keys that
   change which combat zone you are in only work while the Combat
   panel is open, so a stray number key cannot drop you into a
   boss zone from another screen; there is a Settings toggle for
   that if you want them everywhere.
patches.title: Keyboard shortcuts
Big Bang and travel achievements
Buildings that keep paying after you leave

patches.desc:
Late in the game the screen hitches every second or so, worse
   with many jobs running. The cause is the drop roll: every
   enemy you kill makes the game read every card's drop chance
   from text and work it out again from scratch, which throws
   away about 10 MB of memory per kill. Cleaning that up is
   the hitch you see. This remembers each answer the first
   time it is worked out and hands it back after that, and
   lets the text reader keep the patterns it uses instead of
   rebuilding them. Drop chances, enemy stats and bonuses come
   out exactly the same; it was checked against every battle
   zone at every level. Can be turned off in
   BepInEx\config\sti.community.formulacache.cfg.
patches.title: Performance: the stutter while your fleet fights

patches.desc:
Under Techno, the Completion / Cost / Bonus filters on the
   Research and Infrastructure tabs reset to 'All' every time
   you start the game, so if you play with Completion set to
   'Not Max Level' to see what is left to do, you have to set
   it again every session. The base game does save your
   choice - it is reading it back that fails - so this just
   re-applies what your save already contains, a moment after
   the save has finished loading.
   The Effect and Rarity filters on the Deck and Permanent
   card tabs have the same bug and get the same fix. Their
   Tier filter is worse off - the base game never saves it at
   all - so this also starts saving it, into two fields your
   save file has always carried unused. Can be turned off in
   BepInEx\config\sti.community.filtermemory.cfg.
patches.title: Bugfix: filters forget themselves on load

patches.desc:
A trip to one of the outer planets takes real days, and the base
   game lands you with every research, every building and every
   collector switched off - so the flight is followed by a long
   manual setup pass before anything starts earning again. This
   starts them for you the moment you land, including when you
   landed while the game was closed.
   It covers the other three moments the game leaves you
   switched off too: setting off, since the spaceship has its
   own research, buildings and collectors and a flight is the
   longest idle stretch in the game; a Big Bang, including the
   very reset you buy the upgrade on, from the moment you press
   Confirm on the upgrades; and anything that unlocks
   later, which starts on its own as it appears rather than
   waiting for your next flight.
   How much it does is bought in the Big Bang tree, on the new
   'Automated Arrival' line, so it is earned rather than free:
     Level 1 - start every research, building and collector
               that is unlocked, unfinished and not already
               running
     Level 2 - also leave alone any building whose running cost
               your energy income cannot cover, so landing
               somewhere can never put you into a deficit
     Level 3 - also order the new jobs, putting the ones that
               unlock new resources, buildings and research
               first, and keep the priority list feeding
               downwards: energy production at the top, then
               resource production, then research and
               buildings, with the engine right at the
               bottom. Accumulation Layers stay where you put
               them and nothing crosses one except an engine
               module, which always goes below them all
     Level 4 - also carry the whole priority list through a Big
               Bang: the Accumulation Layers, the limits you
               set on them, and which research, buildings and
               collectors sat under which layer. The layers
               come back straight away and everything else
               returns to its old place as it becomes
               available again. Anything you drag afterwards
               becomes the new arrangement. The record itself is
               kept from the moment you install this, at any
               level and with the toggle either way, in a text
               file next to your save - so you can Big Bang now,
               buy the level whenever you can afford it, and the
               arrangement you had is still there
   Want the fuel tank to fill itself? Turn on 'Fill the
   tank' in Settings - it is the one switch that ships
   off, because a filling tank eats your whole energy bank until
   it is full. Put an Accumulation Layer above the modules first
   and the layer holds them back.
   Landing somewhere switches every engine module off and
   forgets what you had them set to - that is the base game. The
   mod now puts them back at the percentage you chose, and with
   level 3 they sit below your Accumulation Layers so the tank
   refills out of what everything else has finished with.
   Each level you own adds its own toggle to the Settings
   panel, under 'Auto start' in the left hand column, so you can
   keep the upgrade and still switch any part of it off. Hover
   over a toggle to see what it does. A level you have not
   bought has no toggle.
   It never touches a job that is already running, never moves
   anything you put in order yourself. A job it starts for the
   first time goes into the main list rather than below your
   Accumulation Layers, where the game itself would put it.
   A building you switched off stays off.
   Because it keeps watching rather than firing once, it
   also never restarts something it has already started - turn a
   job off and it stays off. That slate is wiped when you
   arrive, set off or Big Bang, so each of those still gets a
   clean full pass. Needs the 'more Big Bang upgrades' data patch above for
   the upgrade line to exist; without it you can still turn the
   feature on by hand with the Level setting in
   BepInEx\config\sti.community.autostart.cfg.
   The spaceship's own research, buildings and collectors are
   kept at the bottom of the priority list, just above your
   engine modules, with the four multi-day ones below the rest -
   the spaceship is the one place you never leave, so its jobs
   would otherwise take energy and resources off the planet you
   are trying to finish. And BLACKHOLE is never started for you:
   it costs 1e25 energy and does nothing yet.
patches.title: Start a planet up by itself

patches.desc:
Before a resource collector is allowed to run, the game checks
   whether there is room for a whole BAR's output - not a tick's -
   so a collector goes quiet up to a full bar short of your
   discard/lock line and parks there. Being turned away also resets
   its progress bar to zero, so every tick it waits it throws away
   energy you already spent.
   Collectors now run until the tank is actually at the line; a
   delivery that does not fit is trimmed to the room available
   rather than discarded; and whatever was not delivered stays on
   the bar. Sitting on a full tank costs nothing, and spending
   something picks the collector up where it paused. Offline
   catch-up and energy plants are untouched. There is a toggle
   for it in the game's own Settings panel, and the same switch
   in BepInEx\config\sti.community.topoff.cfg.
patches.title: Collectors fill the tank right to the top

patches.desc:
The 12 new upgrade lines have no artwork in the base game, so
   they all show the same grey 'no image' placeholder. This gives
   each of them its own icon, drawn in the game's own style.
   The icons are ordinary PNG files in
   BepInEx\plugins\bigbang_icons, named after the upgrade, so
   you can replace any of them with your own - and dropping in a
   file named after one of the game's own upgrades replaces that
   one too.
   Needs the 'more Big Bang upgrades' data patch above, since
   without it those upgrades do not exist. On its own it changes
   nothing.
patches.title: Icons for the new Big Bang upgrades

patches.desc:
Storm Core has no picture in the base game - it is a real card
   that really drops, and out of all 52 cards it is the only one
   whose artwork was never drawn, so it shows as an empty frame.
   This gives it one, in the game's own card style, and does the
   same for Lightning Mastery, which had been borrowing Lightning
   Action's picture.
   The pictures are ordinary PNG files in
   BepInEx\plugins\card_icons, named after the card, so you can
   replace them with your own - and dropping in a file named
   after one of the game's own cards replaces that one too.
   Needs nothing else installed. A card with no file keeps the
   picture it has today.
patches.title: Artwork for cards that never had any
Cargo you can actually fly with
